s01.narration: Want everything that's waiting for you at work in one place every morning? Hi, I'm Maria from the Sloneek team, and I'll walk you through the dashboard.

s02.narration: You can open the dashboard any time from the left menu with the Dashboard item, right at the top.

s03.narration: At the top a greeting welcomes you, and below it are cards in two columns, whose content depends on your role.

s04.narration: The first card, On your plate, gathers everything that's waiting for you.

s05.narration: There are requests to approve, assets to handle, tasks with a deadline, documents or feedback.

s06.narration: I click the row with requests to approve, and the card switches to the Approvals list.

s07.narration: Requests are split into tabs, such as absence, activities, attendance or change of personal data.

s08.narration: For each request you see who submitted it and for when, and you can handle it right away with the Approve or Reject button.

s09.narration: The Go to section link leads to the Approvals module, but I'll go back with the left arrow.

s10.narration: Below it is the Feed, the company board, where you'll find announcements from management and kudos from colleagues.

s11.narration: I click the Announcement toggle, and only company announcements remain.

s12.narration: An important announcement can be pinned to the top, and under every post you can react with an emoji or write a comment.

s13.narration: I click New announcement, where an administrator chooses who the message is for and writes its text.

s14.narration: The announcement would reach all recipients by email and in the app, so I won't send it now and click Cancel.

s15.narration: With the Give kudos button you publicly praise a colleague, and with the All toggle I go back to all posts.

s16.narration: The Overview - Today card shows who's away today, and clicking the Home office tab shows who's working from home.

s17.narration: The overview for the next fourteen days shows who'll be away soon, and below it you'll find upcoming birthdays and work anniversaries.

s18.narration: At the top of the right column you'll see new colleagues who recently joined the company.

s19.narration: The mood meter asks every day how you like your work, and you answer with a single click on an emoji.

s20.narration: The Attendance card shows your status today, the Clock in button starts your working day, and below it you'll find your working hours.

s21.narration: The Absences card shows your remaining time off and your upcoming leave.

s22.narration: I click Add absence, and the same request form opens as in the Absence module.

s23.narration: I won't send the request now, so I close the form with the cross.

s24.narration: Similarly, with the Add activity button you log, for example, a meeting or work on a project.

s25.narration: My tasks shows your upcoming tasks, and the arrow next to the heading takes you to the whole section.

s26.narration: Useful links lead to company pages that your administrator has prepared for you.

s27.narration: Team attendance shows managers how many hours their people have worked so far this month.

s28.narration: The last card shows company wiki pages marked as important, and I open one with a click.

s29.narration: You read the article right on the dashboard, and when you're done, you close it with the cross.

s30.narration: Everyone adjusts the layout themselves, so at the top I click the pencil, Customize view.

s31.narration: You drag cards by the handle to another place or to the other column, and clicking the eye hides a card, for example Upcoming anniversaries.

s32.narration: You would confirm the changes with the Save button, but I click Cancel and the dashboard stays unchanged.

s33.narration: Administrators also have a Settings gear next to it, which I click.

s34.narration: On the General tab you hide the mood meter, birthdays or anniversaries for the whole company, and you can forbid users from hiding selected cards.

s35.narration: I click the Useful links tab and then Add link.

s36.narration: In Title I type Newcomer guide, and in the URL field I paste the Help Center address.

s37.narration: I click Save, and the link appears in the list, where you edit it with the pencil or delete it with the bin.

s38.narration: In the left menu I click Dashboard, and the new link is already on the Useful links card.

s39.narration: Now you know what the dashboard shows you, how to handle what's waiting for you, and how to customize it, and if something doesn't work, check the Help Center.

s40.narration: Less admin, more time for people. This is Sloneek.
